questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always had an interest in Italy. Both culturally and historically i find Italy to be a fascinating nation. This is the birthplace of the Roman Empire, The renaissance, Pizza, Calcio and many more things. Therefore the choice of Italy as my destination was not difficult. Furthermore Italy is a popular destination, with many students studying there. For this reason I was not in doubt.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. It could have been better, but everytime i texted the administration they were quick to respond accurately and well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I felt you primarily had to seek out assistance yourself but every time you asked you were always met with helpful people and there were not many problems regarding the arrangement of my stay.

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did not myself find the apartment as my roommate was able to find an apartment quickly. We had no problem and we lived close to City Life.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do it through an agency. It gives you much more security regarding the rent, deposit and other factors of importance to foreign students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Milan is one of the best geographically located cities in Europe. Visit as many citiies as you can, and especeially don't forget the smaller and less popular, towns like Pavia, Lecco, Brescia, Piacenza.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy. If you go in with a great mentality and try to speak a few words of Italian people become the most helpful and nice ones.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and don't be afraid to approach students of different nationalities, more often than not they also want to meet and get to know you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I have southern european heritage, so I found the Italian mentality to be similar to my own. For that reason I have a somewhat hard time to say what would be difficult for a northern european student to adjust to in Italy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and the fact that everyone seemed to be talkative and social at any time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try as many courses as you can before making your final decision. 

Eat a lot of food, but don't forget to mix it up (don't just eat pizza and pasta) 

Have an open mind and enjoy the stay. 

Bonus: Remember that you are not a tourist while you are there, you are a local to some degree. Act like a local as much as you can and try to learn from them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friendships and the fact that I learned a lot of new things, both social and professional.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the initial adjustment in the first 2 weeks. But an open mind makes the transition much easier and better.
